rules.name: TGA Prescription-Only Classification for Hydroquinone > 2%
rules.title: TGA Prescription-Only Classification for Hydroquinone > 2%
rules.directive_code: Poisons Standard (SUSMP) Schedule 4 / Therapeutic Goods Act 1989
rules.statute_citation: Poisons Standard (SUSMP) Schedule 4 / Therapeutic Goods Act 1989
rules.expected_requirement: Hydroquinone concentrations exceeding 2.0% are classified as Schedule 4 Prescription Only Medicines and cannot be sold OTC in Australia.
rules.explanation: Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration strictly restricts hydroquinone in cosmetics. Over 2% requires an Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) inclusion and prescription dispensation.
rules.fix_suggestion: Cap hydroquinone concentration at <= 2.0% or register as a prescription medicine on the ARTG.

rules.name: Mandatory Australian INCI Ingredient Labeling Standard
rules.title: Mandatory Australian INCI Ingredient Labeling Standard
rules.directive_code: Competition and Consumer Act 2010 - Consumer Protection Notice No. 1 of 2020
rules.statute_citation: Competition and Consumer Act 2010 - Consumer Protection Notice No. 1 of 2020
rules.expected_requirement: All cosmetic ingredients must be clearly listed on the product container or packaging using INCI nomenclature in descending order of volume/weight.
rules.explanation: ACCC mandatory standard for cosmetics ingredient labeling requires complete disclosure of all ingredients on retail packaging.
rules.fix_suggestion: Provide a complete list of ingredients in descending order of prominence using standard INCI names.

rules.name: Prohibited Therapeutic Disease Treatment Claims
rules.title: Prohibited Therapeutic Disease Treatment Claims
rules.expected_requirement: Therapeutic representations cannot be made on cosmetic goods without formal TGA ARTG registration.
rules.explanation: Claiming to cure or treat arthritis or serious medical conditions reclassifies the cosmetic as an unapproved therapeutic good under Australian federal law.
rules.fix_suggestion: Change curative claims to soothing or cosmetic structure/function claims, or secure ARTG inclusion.

requirements.name: TGA ARTG Inclusion Certificate
requirements.description: Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods listing.

rules.name: Mandatory Safety Standard for Toys for Children up to 36 Months
rules.title: Mandatory Safety Standard for Toys for Children up to 36 Months
rules.directive_code: Consumer Goods (Toys for Children up to and including 36 Months of Age) Safety Standard 2023 / AS/NZS ISO 8124.1
rules.statute_citation: Consumer Goods (Toys for Children up to and including 36 Months of Age) Safety Standard 2023 / AS/NZS ISO 8124.1
rules.expected_requirement: Toys for children under 3 must not pose choking hazards, small parts, or sharp edges under AS/NZS ISO 8124.1.
rules.explanation: Supplying non-compliant toys in Australia breaches Section 106 of the Australian Consumer Law, attracting heavy penalties up to AUD $10M for corporations.
rules.fix_suggestion: Ensure toys undergo mechanical safety testing against AS/NZS ISO 8124.1 and do not liberate small parts.

rules.name: Mandatory Safety Standard for Baby Walkers (Stair Fall Prevention)
rules.title: Mandatory Safety Standard for Baby Walkers (Stair Fall Prevention)
rules.directive_code: Consumer Protection Notice No. 1 of 2013 / AS 4684:2009
rules.statute_citation: Consumer Protection Notice No. 1 of 2013 / AS 4684:2009
rules.expected_requirement: Baby walkers must be fitted with friction gripping mechanisms to stop the walker at a step or drop-off under AS 4684.
rules.explanation: While not banned outright like in Canada, baby walkers in Australia must strictly comply with stair-fall prevention mechanism testing.
rules.fix_suggestion: Provide test report showing compliance with AS 4684:2009 friction pad and stair drop-off tests.

rules.name: Regulatory Compliance Mark (RCM) for Electrical Equipment
rules.title: Regulatory Compliance Mark (RCM) for Electrical Equipment
rules.expected_requirement: Rechargeable electronic consumer products must comply with Australian electrical safety and EMC standards and bear the RCM mark.
rules.explanation: Supplying in-scope electrical equipment without registration on the national EESS database or without the RCM mark is unlawful.
rules.fix_suggestion: Test against relevant AS/NZS standards, register with EESS, and affix the RCM mark.

requirements.name: Regulatory Compliance Mark (RCM)
requirements.description: RCM mark on device and packaging.
